definitions.explanation: A vivid reddish-orange color, traditionally associated with the pigment made from cinnabar. A characteristic color of Japanese shrines and traditional lacquerware.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{朱色|しゅいろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{塗|ぬ}られている→塗る：01174_nuru⟧。
examples.english: The torii gate is painted vermillion.

examples.japanese: {朱色|しゅいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{漆器|しっき}→漆器：13329_shikki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: Vermillion lacquerware is lined up on the table.

examples.japanese: ⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木々|きぎ}→木々：04811_kigi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{朱色|しゅいろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まって→染まる：04254_somaru⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
examples.english: In autumn, the mountain trees turn vermillion and look beautiful.

notes:
A vivid reddish-orange color with deep roots in Japanese culture. Composed of ⟦{朱|しゅ}→朱：24206_shu⟧ (vermillion) + ⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧ (color). The pigment was originally derived from cinnabar ({辰砂|しんしゃ}), a mercury sulfide mineral.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朱色|しゅいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧: vermillion torii gate
- {朱色|しゅいろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{塗|ぬ}る→塗る：01174_nuru⟧: to paint vermillion
- {朱色|しゅいろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧: to turn vermillion
- ⟦{鮮|あざ}やか→鮮やか：05702_azayaka⟧な{朱色|しゅいろ}: vivid vermillion

CULTURAL NOTE:
Vermillion is one of the most iconic colors in Japanese culture. Shinto shrine gates (⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧), temple buildings, and traditional lacquerware frequently feature this color. It is believed to ward off evil spirits and symbolize vitality and prosperity. The ⟦{朱|しゅ}{肉|にく}→朱肉：06192_shuniku⟧ (vermillion ink pad) used for seals (⟦{印鑑|いんかん}→印鑑：05290_inkan⟧) also uses this color.
